source.spoken_script: # The Seed of the Woman — long-form narration (DRAFT v1.2) **Series:** types-shadows (#3) · **Format:** 16:9, ~6–8 min, 7-movement spine **Core text:** Genesis 3:8–19 (the protoevangelium, 3:15) · **NT trajectory (not verbatim quotation):** Galatians 4:4 · Romans 16:20 · Hebrews 2:14 · Colossians 2:15 · 1 John 3:8 · Revelation 12:9–11 · Luke 1:35 **Thread (one spine, hook→landing — C-led, panel-locked):** When the world breaks in Eden, God's very first word of consequence is not a threat to the guilty couple — it is a promise of rescue, spoken *to the serpent*, hidden inside his curse, before Adam or Eve are sentenced. And that promise tells the whole story in advance: a deliverer is coming, the woman's seed, who will crush the enemy by taking the enemy's own deadly blow. The hook (the first gospel, preached to the snake) is paid off at the landing (the serpent's head crushed at the cross, and his end still "shortly" coming). **Status:** DRAFT v1.1 — thread LOCKED via `/study` + 5-CLI panel (`_thread_LOCKED.md`; panel flipped the original A+B pick to C-led, raw reviews in `_independent_review\20260624-101655\`). **Narration 5-CLI panel DONE** (`_independent_review\20260624-105959\`: cursor/claude/codex/grok all REVISE, convergent; gemini env-failed). Applied all convergent fixes: (1) Col 2:15 → restored leading **"And"** (KJV-exact); (2) chronology — M3 now anchors the hook to the *sentencing* order (3:15 before the sentences on Eve/Adam), not "first words after the fall"; removed M2's premature Gen 3:19 quote; (3) M5 — added the 4th steel-man objection ("her seed" is ordinary — Hagar/Rebekah) + softened the NT-tracing overclaim; (4) M7 — dropped the banned generic "trust Him" close, re-landed on the serpent-addressed promise ("step out from behind the trees… be found by Him"), kept the already/not-yet ("end is now only a matter of time"); (5) M4 — dropped the singular-"it" grammar lean, added Luke 1:35, softened "reaches back/money in the bank"; (6) M2 — removed "joined the rebellion/changed sides" (no Satan read into the Eden moment). **v1.2 — RE-PANELED UNBIASED** (clean artifact, no context/status leak, `_independent_review\20260624-120700\`: claude PASS, cursor/codex REVISE; gemini/grok env-failed). Applied convergent fixes: (a) **M3** — 3:14 is curse, the promise (3:15) is woven in *before* the human sentences (was "the first words of judgment are a promise"); (b) **M6 Col 2:15** re-anchored to the CROSS ("the victory was won *in* the cross"), empty tomb now only "put it beyond doubt" (was mis-pinned to the resurrection); (c) **M5** thinned the 4-objection lecture-stack to 2, answered in flow (by-ear clarity); (d) "Page three" → "the opening pages"; (e) **M7** "head is broken" → already/not-yet consistent, "set his prisoners free"→"free those he held by sin and death", "took his side"→"before you were ever born", "not waiting to sentence you"→"did not come to sentence you"; (f) softened clickbait M3 opener, removed the non-KJV "fulfilled today" quote, "heel got up"→"rose". **NOTE: v1.1 audio (narration.mp3) is now STALE — text changed; needs re-synth before the visual stage.** Panel constraints baked in: (1) C-led — hook rests on the plain narrative order, not a contestable grammar claim; (2) "her seed" is an *unusual clue*, NOT a virgin-birth grammatical proof — no "only/everywhere/always", no sinlessness-via-bypassing-male-descent; (3) M4/M5 are honest that **no NT writer quotes Gen 3:15 verbatim** — trajectory + NT application, never "explicit citation"; (4) KJV-strict **"it shall bruise thy head"** (never "he"); (5) M6 names the **penal** exchange (sin/death borne), with resurrection + a future ("shortly") dimension, not combat-metaphor alone; (6) serpent = Satan stated as **canonical** theology (Rev 12:9), not read back into the Eden text. Multi-voice: **the_LORD** voices Gen 3:14–15. **v1.3 (2026-07-03): RE-PANELED on the repaired FULL 5/5 panel** (`_independent_review\20260703-061152\`: claude PASS, rest REVISE, n

platforms.description:

"And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." (Genesis 3:15)

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: The Oldest Prophecy of Jesus -- Hidden in a Curse (Genesis 3:15)
platforms.description:
In the moment everything breaks in Eden, God speaks -- and His first words aren't judgment on the man and the woman. They're a promise, spoken to the serpent, hidden inside a curse:

"And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." (Genesis 3:15)

This single verse -- the first messianic prophecy in the Bible -- names a coming deliverer before Adam and Eve are even sentenced. The woman's seed will crush the serpent's head; the serpent will only manage to bruise his heel. A costly victory, promised before the fall's consequences are even spoken.

This deep-dive traces that promise forward -- through its echoes in Galatians, Romans, Hebrews, Colossians, 1 John, and Revelation -- to the cross, where the enemy's defeat was finally accomplished, and the empty tomb, which put that victory beyond doubt.

The whole Bible is one story. It starts here, in a garden, with a promise spoken to a snake -- and it is still true today: the seed of the woman has crushed the head of the enemy, and His victory is not waiting to be won. It is already won. Step out from hiding, and be found by Him.

Core text: Genesis 3:8-19

gates.detail: youtube_short: anchor ref 'genesis' not in the first 157 chars (front-load the verse/hook before the 'more' fold); youtube_long: anchor ref 'genesis' not in the first 157 chars (front-load the verse/hook before the 'more' fold); facebook: anchor ref 'genesis' not in the first 157 chars (front-load the verse/hook before the 'more' fold)

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- KJV check: the quoted verse ("And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.") is verbatim and identical across every platform that quotes it in full (youtube_short, youtube_long, instagram); facebook quotes a shorter exact substring ("it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel") which is also a clean verbatim fragment, correctly attributed to Genesis 3:15. No paraphrase-as-quote anywhere.
- Clickbait check: "spoken to a snake" is not a curiosity-gap lie -- Genesis 3:15 is literally addressed to the serpent, and this is the video's actual stated thread (the promise precedes the human sentencing). "The first prophecy of Jesus" / "the first gospel" (protoevangelium) is a real, mainstream theological designation for this verse, not an invented overclaim.
- Off-thread check: every platform's copy stays on the single thread (promise-before-judgment, spoken to the serpent, fulfilled at the cross) -- no platform promises content (e.g. a debunking angle, a different verse, a different payoff) the video doesn't deliver.
- Banned-phrase check: none of the constitution's banned openers ("Did you know...", "Have you ever wondered...", "hidden secret...", "the real meaning of...") or banned CTA tropes ("Drop a comment if...", "Like and follow for more") appear anywhere in the drafted copy.
- Platform-fit check: TikTok leads with the hook in the first line and stays punchy; YouTube long has the fuller apologetic/deep-dive register the series calls for; titles avoid the generic auto-complete ("the crucifixion" centred only on physical suffering, etc.) the constitution specifically bans for this kind of topic.
- One structural flag, not a copywriting defect: every stamped footer in this kit ("Find Jesus in the whole Bible, one panel at a time...✝") includes a non-ASCII cross glyph. If UK-G7's plain-ASCII anti-slop check is meant to cover the FULL rendered description (footer included, not just the drafted body), this will need checking against data/upload_brand.json -- that's a footer-stamping question, not something the auto-draft controls, but worth confirming before the gate runs.
- Also worth a human sanity check, not a fail: the brand footer's "one panel at a time" phrasing describes a comic-panel visual style; this piece is a painted living-sketchbook long-form, not comic panels. Likely just a fixed cross-format brand tagline (fine if so) -- flagging so a human can confirm it's intentional rather than a copy-paste mismatch from a different content line.

No REVISE-worthy findings. The kit is honest, on-thread, KJV-exact, and does not oversell.
